claim_text: Transition temperature rises and the transition window narrows as domain size grows

steps.observation: Every trace steps down near 150 K; for PC (004) the two branches coexist over a shaded band from ~150 to ~175 K
steps.image_note: the regime labels 'orthorhombic' and 'tetragonal(224)' are written along the bottom axis of F2a; the coexistence band is highlighted in yellow

panels.caption_span: Temperature-dependent XRD 2theta peaks of SC (blue color), PC (red color), and HOC (black color) perovskites in the range from 40.5 to 42.5 . Visual illustration of
panels.layer_why: saturation split caught the whole layer; clean panel handed over, masked regions declared

steps.contribution_why: The observation documents a step near 150 K in every trace and a coexistence band (~150-175 K) for one case (PC (004)), which is consistent with the existence of a transition temperature and a finite transition window, but it reports data for a single domain size rather than comparing multiple domain sizes, so it does not itself show that the transition temperature rises or that the window narrows as domain size grows.
unsettled: comparison of transition temperature across different domain sizes
comparison of transition window width across different domain sizes
whether the trend is monotonic with domain size
whether other traces besides PC (004) also show a comparable coexistence band

steps.observation: PL at 80 K: one ~790 nm band for D_d of 20-50 nm, two bands (~750 and ~785 nm) for 50-200 um, one ~750 nm band above 300 um
steps.image_note: nine stacked spectra labelled D_d < 20 nm to > 500 um with an arrow 'Domain size decrease'; D_d = 1 and 10 um are single broad asymmetric bands, D_d = 300 and 400 um a sharp 750 nm peak with a weak shoulder

panels.caption_span: PL spectra at 80K for MAPb|3 perovskites of different domain-sizes
panels.layer_why: the observation is read from the author's annotation, so masking it would overlap the graded feature; the author's label is the claim under test instead

steps.contribution_why: The observation shows that at a single fixed temperature (80 K) the PL signature shifts from one band (small domains) to two coexisting bands (intermediate domains) to one band again (large domains), which is consistent with domain size shifting the phase-transition/coexistence region, but it provides no temperature-scan data to quantify that the transition temperature actually rises or that the transition window narrows with increasing domain size.
unsettled: quantitative transition temperature values across domain sizes
direct measurement of transition window width (temperature range) for each domain size
confirmation that the two-band region corresponds to the transition window rather than a static structural difference
temperature dependence beyond the single 80 K snapshot

steps.observation: Emission-regime map: single orthorhombic at low T and large domains, single tetragonal at high T, a dual band between that widens toward small domains
steps.image_note: smoothed drawn summary with no data points or contour values; temperature axis runs downward from ~90 K to ~190 K; the dual/tetragonal boundary sits near 150-157 K at 5e2 um and the tetragonal field reaches ~105-110 K near zero domain size

panels.caption_span: Contour map of the phase-transition process as a function of domain-size for MAPb|3 from 80 to 90K
panels.layer_why: the observation is read from the author's annotation, so masking it would overlap the graded feature; the author's label is the claim under test instead

steps.contribution_why: The map directly shows the dual-band transition window widening toward small domains (equivalently narrowing as domains grow), but it only implies rather than directly quantifies that the transition temperature itself shifts upward with increasing domain size.
unsettled: explicit rise of the transition temperature (not just window width) as a function of domain size
quantitative relationship or threshold between domain size and transition temperature

steps.observation: In F5a the 300 and 400 um spectra are already single orthorhombic peaks, so dual emission ends between 200 and 300 um, not above 500 um
steps.image_note: linked text says dual emission runs from 1 to 300 um and a single orthorhombic peak appears only above 500 um; D_d = 1 and 10 um also look single and broad rather than dual

steps.contribution_why: The observation pins down the domain-size threshold at which dual emission collapses into a single peak (between 200-300 um rather than above 500 um), supporting the window-narrowing part of the claim but saying nothing about whether transition temperature itself rises with domain size.
unsettled: transition temperature rising with domain size
precise onset point of narrowing below 200 um
whether narrowing is monotonic across the full size range
